originalTitle: Riot is ending development on its League of Legends fighting game
summary: Riot Games is already winding down work on 2XKO, the free-to-play League of Legends fighting game, less than a year after its initial launch. content: Riot Games is already winding down work on 2XKO, the free-to-play League of Legends fighting game, less than a year after its initial launch. Riot says “active development” will conclude at the end of 2026 because the company hasn’t “seen enough players stick with the game to get to a path toward sustainability.” Servers will stay online “beyond 2026,” and Riot is unlocking all playable characters and refunding money spent on the game. 2XKO launched in an early access beta on PC in October 2025 and hit PS5 and Xbox Series X / S in January. But shortly after, Riot announced it would be cutting staff working on the game, saying at the time that “overall momentum hasn’t reached the level needed to support a team of this size long term.”  It seems like things never turned a corner. Riot says in its Thursday announcement that it evaluated the game’s overall performance through the year, and while there were some bright spots with new character releases and competitive events, it wasn’t enough to keep the game going. “Even in these highlight moments, however, we saw no meaningful, sustained change in 2XKO’s trajectory; only a fraction of what it would take to trend toward sustainability,” Riot says. “Over time it became clear it would be impossible for us to continue actively developing the game as we are today.” Riot says it would have continued development if “we saw any viable future,” but notes that “2XKO costs us substantially more to operate than it brings in, and engagement has stayed relatively flat despite our larger updates.” 2XKO is just the latest big live service bet that hasn’t panned out. Just this week, Bloomberg reported that Sony is stripping live service elements from its in-development multiplayer Horizon title. Highguard, following its closing announcement at December’s Game Awards, permanently shut down less than two months after launch. Earlier this year, Remedy announced a final major update for FBC: Firebreak, its live service shooter set in the Control universe — though like Riot’s plan for 2XKO, Remedy has chosen to keep Firebreak online. Even Fortnite isn’t immune to problems, as developer Epic Games laid off staff in March following a “downturn in Fortnite engagement.”

chineseContent: Riot Games 已经开始结束免费英雄联盟格斗游戏 2XKO 的开发工作，距其首次推出还不到一年。 Riot 表示，“积极开发”将于 2026 年底结束，因为该公司“还没有看到足够多的玩家坚持游戏以走上可持续发展的道路”。服务器将在“2026 年之后”保持在线状态，Riot 正在解锁所有可玩角色并退还游戏费用。 2XKO 于 2025 年 10 月在 PC 上推出抢先体验测试版，并于 1 月登陆 PS5 和 Xbox Series X/S。但不久之后，Riot 宣布将裁员该游戏的工作人员，当时表示“整体势头尚未达到长期支持如此规模团队所需的水平。”  事情似乎从未出现转机。 Riot在周四的公告中表示，它评估了游戏全年的整体表现，虽然新角色发布和竞技活动有一些亮点，但这还不足以让游戏继续下去。 “然而，即使在这些高光时刻，我们也没有看到 2XKO 的发展轨迹发生任何有意义的、持续的变化；只是走向可持续发展所需的一小部分，”Riot 说。 “随着时间的推移，我们发现我们不可能像今天这样继续积极开发游戏。” Riot表示，如果“我们看到任何可行的未来”，它就会继续发展，但他指出，“2XKO的运营成本远高于其带来的收入，尽管我们进行了较大的更新，但参与度仍保持相对平稳。” 2XKO只是最新的一场尚未成功的大型现场发球赌注。就在本周，彭博社报道称，索尼正在从其正在开发的多人游戏《地平线》中剥离实时服务元素。 Highguard，在其关闭公告之后
